newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Brittan-EU, US "long way" from Helms-Burton deal.
newsitem.headline: Brittan-EU, US "long way" from Helms-Burton deal.

text.p: EU Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan said on Friday that the European Union and United States were a "long way" from reaching a deal in their dispute over the U.S. Helms-Burton act penalising foreign investment in Cuba.

He also told a briefing in Geneva that the EU was is in intensive discussions with the U.S. to try to find a solution to meet "European concerns." If such a solution were found, the EU would drop its World Trade Organisation (WTO) case against Washington, Brittan indicated.
"I have to say that so far, we are not close to a deal that meets European concerns...We are really quite a long way from it," Brittan said.

The EU and the United States have been at odds for nearly a year over the act, which penalises foreign companies that benefit from investments in property confiscated from U.S. citizens by Havana since the 1959 communist revolution.
The two sides have been unable to agree on the composition of the panel.
Brittan said Wednesday he had asked WTO chief Renato Ruggiero to delay naming a panel to make the ruling until February 20 in a bid to reach a settlement with Washington over the Helms-Burton Act.
